decisions.source_name: IPNI duplicate citations for Muhlenbergia lindheimeri Hitchc.
decisions.reason: IPNI 164816-2 and 409064-1 are linked as the same 1934 publication citation, not two taxon concepts. Canonical POWO identifier is 164816-2.

decisions.source_name: IPNI duplicate citations for Muhlenbergia reverchonii
decisions.reason: IPNI 164871-2 lists the 409132-1 'Vasey & Scribn. ex Vasey' rendering as SAME CITATION. Retain author-qualified alternate source string; POWO accepted citation remains Vasey & Scribn.

decisions.source_name: Automatic synonymizing Epicampes gracilis with Muhlenbergia gracilis
decisions.reason: The synonym Epicampes gracilis Trin. maps to M. lindheimeri, while M. gracilis (Kunth) Kunth maps to accepted M. quadridentata; 'gracilis' alone is insufficient to determine identity.

decisions.source_name: Podosemum reverchonii as a separately accepted species
decisions.reason: The 1921 combination is a homotypic synonym of existing M. reverchonii; a separate canonical species would duplicate the accepted concept.

decisions.source_name: Reassigning either parent species record to M. × involuta from intermediate habit
decisions.reason: Accepted hybrid formula does not synonymize either parent or identify a specimen. Existing species and hybrid canonical records must stay separate.

decisions.source_name: Existing parent-species gallery specimens and observations
decisions.reason: Name-only review did not examine individual vouchers or source photograph pixels. Do not elevate labels to confirmed IDs or remove existing scientific holds.
POWO accepted named-hybrid parentage is taxon-level. It does not demonstrate parentage, genetic ancestry or provenance of any particular photographed plant.

decisions.source_name: Unqualified historic 'gracilis' or 'reverchonii' record without genus/author/voucher
decisions.reason: Multiple author-qualified historical names and duplicate IPNI citation strings exist. Do not normalize an authorless or voucherless historical record to a species or hybrid without its original combination and supporting context.
